q: The Law of Conservation of Energy states that in any physical or chemical process, energy can neither be created nor _____.
e: The Law of Conservation of Energy states that in any physical or chemical process, energy can neither be created nor destroyed. Transformed: transformation is one form changing into another, with energy conserved. Transferred: transfer is energy moving from system to surroundings, still conserved.

q: The process of changing one form of energy into another without a net loss or gain is called energy _____.
e: The process of changing one form of energy into another without a net loss or gain is called energy transformation. Conservation means the total energy stays the same. Dissipation is energy spreading as less useful heat, not the name of the process in this stem.

q: An electric motor transforms electrical energy into _____ energy.
e: An electric motor transforms electrical energy into kinetic energy. Thermal would be waste heat, not the useful output of electric motor. Chemical is stored in fuels or batteries, not produced by electric motor.

q: A hair dryer transforms electrical energy into _____ energy.
e: A hair dryer transforms electrical energy into thermal energy. Kinetic is not the named output of hair dryer. Light is not what hair dryer is designed to produce.

q: A battery transforms chemical energy into _____ energy.
e: A battery transforms chemical energy into electrical energy. Mechanical is not the named output of battery. Kinetic is not the named output of battery.

q: An automobile engine transforms chemical energy into _____ energy.
e: An automobile engine transforms chemical energy into mechanical energy. Electrical is the input, or a different device's output, not what this stem names. Thermal would be waste heat, not the useful output of automobile engine.

q: A solar cell transforms light energy into _____ energy.
e: A solar cell transforms light energy into electrical energy. Chemical energy is stored in bonds. Kinetic energy is energy of motion.

q: Chemical energy is the energy that is stored in the _____ of chemical compounds.
e: Chemical energy is the energy that is stored in the bonds of chemical compounds. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Plants store chemical energy in _____ formed during photosynthesis.
e: Plants store chemical energy in carbohydrates formed during photosynthesis. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: Humans release chemical energy during _____ and use it to power systems inside the body.
e: Humans release chemical energy during digestion and use it to power systems inside the body. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: A process that can take place on its own accord under a given set of conditions is called _____.
e: A process that can take place on its own accord under a given set of conditions is called spontaneous. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive.

q: Non-spontaneous processes need the _____ to take place.
e: Non-spontaneous processes need the energy to take place. Physical state changes still move energy even though the substance stays the same chemically.

q: Adding a solution of dilute sulphuric acid to a solution of sodium hydroxide is an example of a _____ reaction.
e: Adding a solution of dilute sulphuric acid to a solution of sodium hydroxide is an example of a spontaneous reaction. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive.

q: The reaction between magnesium and oxygen needs energy to initiate, so it is a _____ reaction.
e: The reaction between magnesium and oxygen needs energy to initiate, so it is a non-spontaneous reaction. A spontaneous process can proceed on its own under the stated conditions, but that does not always mean it is fast.

q: Iron rusting is exothermic and _____.
e: Iron rusting is exothermic and spontaneous. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive.

q: When ice melts at room temperature, that is a spontaneous and _____ process.
e: When ice melts at room temperature, that is a spontaneous and endothermic process. Exothermic means heat is given out and delta H is negative. Isothermal: thermal energy is heat.

q: When sulphuric acid is slowly poured into water, the flask becomes hot because heat is _____ to the surroundings.
e: When sulphuric acid is slowly poured into water, the flask becomes hot because heat is released to the surroundings. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Which of the following is an example of an exothermic reaction?
e: Which of the following is an example of an exothermic reaction? An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: In an exothermic reaction, the energy of the product is _____ than the energy of the reactants.
e: In an exothermic reaction, the energy of the product is lower than the energy of the reactants. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: Exothermic reactions give out energy, so there is a temperature _____ in the surroundings.
e: Exothermic reactions give out energy, so there is a temperature rise in the surroundings. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: When ammonium chloride is dissolved in water, the flask becomes quite cold because heat is _____ from the surroundings.
e: When ammonium chloride is dissolved in water, the flask becomes quite cold because heat is absorbed from the surroundings. The dissolving takes heat in, so it is endothermic.

q: Which of the following is an example of an endothermic reaction?
e: Which of the following is an example of an endothermic reaction? An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: In an endothermic reaction, the energy of the products is _____ than the energy of the reactants.
e: In an endothermic reaction, the energy of the products is lower than the energy of the reactants. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: Endothermic reactions take in energy from the surroundings, so there is a temperature _____.
e: Endothermic reactions take in energy from the surroundings, so there is a temperature fall. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: Energy changes in chemical reactions are caused by the making and _____ of chemical bonds.
e: Energy changes in chemical reactions are caused by the making and breaking of chemical bonds. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In a chemical reaction, energy is _____ to break bonds in the reactants.
e: In a chemical reaction, energy is absorbed to break bonds in the reactants. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Bond breaking is an _____ process.
e: Bond breaking is an endothermic process. Exothermic means heat is given out and delta H is negative. Isothermal: thermal energy is heat.

q: Bond making is an _____ process.
e: Bond making is an exothermic process. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive.

q: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is less than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is _____.
e: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is less than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is exothermic. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive.

q: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is more than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is _____.
e: If the energy absorbed in bond breaking is more than the energy given out in bond making, the reaction is exothermic. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive.

q: Everything in the universe other than the system is called the _____.
e: Everything in the universe other than the system is called the universe. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The specific part of the universe that contains the reaction or process which is studied is called the _____.
e: The specific part of the universe that contains the reaction or process which is studied is called the system. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In an instant cold pack, the temperature change occurs due to a solid substance _____ in water.
e: In an instant cold pack, the temperature change occurs due to a solid substance dissolving in water. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: In an instant hot pack, energy is _____ when bonds are formed during the process.
e: In an instant hot pack, energy is absorbed when bonds are formed during the process. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Chemical reactions provide electricity which is the result of interactions between ions in an _____.
e: Chemical reactions provide electricity which is the result of interactions between ions in an electrolyte. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The total chemical energy of a substance is called its _____.
e: The total chemical energy of a substance is called its enthalpy. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The symbol for enthalpy is _____.
e: The symbol for enthalpy is H. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The unit of enthalpy change is _____.
e: The unit of enthalpy change is extkJmol-1. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The standard pressure chosen for energy changes is $1	ext{ atm}$, which is equal to _____ $	ext{kPa}$.
e: The standard pressure chosen for energy changes is 1extatm, which is equal to 101 extkPa. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: A balanced chemical equation that includes the physical states and standard enthalpy change is called a _____ equation.
e: A balanced chemical equation that includes the physical states and standard enthalpy change is called a thermochemical equation. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The standard enthalpy change of formation is the enthalpy change when _____ of a compound is formed from its elements.
e: The standard enthalpy change of formation is the enthalpy change when one mole of a compound is formed from its elements. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: When writing thermochemical equations for carbon, the most stable form chosen is _____.
e: When writing thermochemical equations for carbon, the most stable form chosen is graphite. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: The standard enthalpy change of combustion is the enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is burnt completely in _____.
e: The standard enthalpy change of combustion is the enthalpy change when one mole of a substance is burnt completely in oxygen. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: Combustion reactions are always exothermic and the enthalpy changes are always _____.
e: Combustion reactions are always exothermic and the enthalpy changes are always positive. An exothermic reaction releases heat to the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is negative.

q: The standard enthalpy change of neutralisation is the enthalpy change when solutions of an acid and an alkali react to produce one mole of _____.
e: The standard enthalpy change of neutralisation is the enthalpy change when solutions of an acid and an alkali react to produce one mole of water. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The neutralisation reaction between a strong acid and strong alkali is exothermic and the enthalpy change is _____.
e: The neutralisation reaction between a strong acid and strong alkali is exothermic and the enthalpy change is positive. A strong acid ionises completely in water, so almost every molecule dumps its proton.

q: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one gram of water by one degree is known as the specific heat _____ of water.
e: The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of one gram of water by one degree is known as the specific heat capacity of water. Specific heat capacity is the energy needed to raise 1 g of a substance by 1 degree Celsius.

q: A device used to measure the amount of heat released or absorbed in reactions that occur in solutions is called a _____.
e: A device used to measure the amount of heat released or absorbed in reactions that occur in solutions is called a calorimeter. A calorimeter measures heat by tracking the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution.

q: In a simple calorimeter, the heat change can be measured through the _____.
e: In a simple calorimeter, the heat change can be measured through the thermometer. A calorimeter measures heat by tracking the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution.

q: A bomb calorimeter is a type of calorimeter for determining the heat of _____ by igniting a sample in a high pressure of oxygen.
e: A bomb calorimeter is a type of calorimeter for determining the heat of combustion by igniting a sample in a high pressure of oxygen. A calorimeter measures heat by tracking the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution.

q: The highly accurate values of the standard enthalpy change of combustion can be measured only by a _____ calorimeter.
e: The highly accurate values of the standard enthalpy change of combustion can be measured only by a bomb calorimeter. A calorimeter measures heat by tracking the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution.

q: A bomb calorimeter is used to measure the energy content of _____.
e: A bomb calorimeter is used to measure the energy content of fuels. A calorimeter measures heat by tracking the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution.

q: The heat change accompanying a chemical reaction at constant pressure is called the _____ change.
e: The heat change accompanying a chemical reaction at constant pressure is called the entropy change. Kinetic energy is energy of motion.

q: In the thermochemical equation $	ext{C} + 	ext{O}_2	ext{(g)} ightarrow 	ext{CO}_2	ext{(g)}$, the state symbol for carbon is written specifically as _____.
e: In the thermochemical equation extC + extO2 ext(g) ightarrow extCO2 ext(g), the state symbol for carbon is written specifically as graphite. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: When calculating enthalpy change of neutralisation in a very dilute solution, its specific heat capacity is taken to be the same as that of _____.
e: When calculating enthalpy change of neutralisation in a very dilute solution, its specific heat capacity is taken to be the same as that of water. Specific heat capacity is the energy needed to raise 1 g of a substance by 1 degree Celsius.

q: In a calorimeter experiment, the mass of water is often used instead of volume because its density is _____ $	ext{g cm}^{-3}$.
e: In a calorimeter experiment, the mass of water is often used instead of volume because its density is 1.00 extgcm-3.

q: The standard conditions chosen for energy changes include a standard pressure of $760$ _____.
e: The standard conditions chosen for energy changes include a standard pressure of 760 extmmHg. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The standard enthalpy change of neutralisation for $	ext{HCl}$ and $	ext{NaOH}$ is approximately $-57.1$ _____ .
e: The standard enthalpy change of neutralisation for extHCl and extNaOH is approximately -57.1 extkJmol-1.

q: The simplest way of measuring enthalpy change is to use the energy to heat or cool _____ or a solution.
e: The simplest way of measuring enthalpy change is to use the energy to heat or cool water or a solution. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: When solid ammonium nitrate is dissolved in water in a calorimeter, the temperature of the water _____ .
e: When solid ammonium nitrate is dissolved in water in a calorimeter, the temperature of the water falls. A calorimeter measures heat by tracking the temperature change of a known mass of water or solution.

q: Enthalpy is not measured directly, however, the change in enthalpy is measured, which is the heat added or lost by the _____.
e: Enthalpy is not measured directly, however, the change in enthalpy is measured, which is the heat added or lost by the system. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: Hess's law states that the enthalpy change for a chemical reaction is the same, whatever _____ is taken from reactants to products.
e: Hess's law states that the enthalpy change for a chemical reaction is the same, whatever route is taken from reactants to products. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: In some cases, a reaction is difficult or impossible to carry out individually, so its enthalpy change can be determined indirectly by using _____ law.
e: In some cases, a reaction is difficult or impossible to carry out individually, so its enthalpy change can be determined indirectly by using Hess's law. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: Hess's law can be illustrated by drawing an enthalpy _____.
e: Hess's law can be illustrated by drawing an enthalpy cycle. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: According to Hess's law, if Route I goes directly from A to B, and Route II goes from A to C then C to B, the enthalpy change of Route I is _____ to Route II.
e: According to Hess's law, if Route I goes directly from A to B, and Route II goes from A to C then C to B, the enthalpy change of Route I is equal to Route II. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The standard enthalpy change for the formation of an element in its standard state is _____.
e: The standard enthalpy change for the formation of an element in its standard state is zero. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: When constructing an enthalpy cycle to find the enthalpy change of reaction from enthalpy changes of formation, the elements are written at the bottom with arrows pointing _____.
e: When constructing an enthalpy cycle to find the enthalpy change of reaction from enthalpy changes of formation, the elements are written at the bottom with arrows pointing upwards. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: To determine the enthalpy change of formation from enthalpy changes of combustion, the combustion products are written at the bottom with arrows pointing _____.
e: To determine the enthalpy change of formation from enthalpy changes of combustion, the combustion products are written at the bottom with arrows pointing upwards. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The combustion products usually considered in Hess's cycles for organic compounds are carbon dioxide and _____.
e: The combustion products usually considered in Hess's cycles for organic compounds are carbon dioxide and water. Hess's law says the overall enthalpy change depends only on start and finish, not on the path you take.

q: The energy needed to make or break bonds is called bond _____ .
e: The energy needed to make or break bonds is called bond energy. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The symbol for bond energy is _____.
e: The symbol for bond energy is E. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The higher the bond enthalpy, the more energy needed to break the bond, and the _____ is the bond.
e: The higher the bond enthalpy, the more energy needed to break the bond, and the stronger is the bond. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: When new bonds are formed, the amount of energy released is the _____ as the amount of energy absorbed when the same type of bond is broken.
e: When new bonds are formed, the amount of energy released is the same as the amount of energy absorbed when the same type of bond is broken. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The bond enthalpies for the breaking and forming bonds of bromine molecules are $+193	ext{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ and _____ $	ext{kJ mol}^{-1}$, respectively.
e: The bond enthalpies for the breaking and forming bonds of bromine molecules are +193extkJmol-1 and -193 extkJmol-1, respectively. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Hess's law can be used to find approximate values of enthalpy change of a reaction using bond _____.
e: Hess's law can be used to find approximate values of enthalpy change of a reaction using bond enthalpies. Enthalpy change is the heat absorbed or released by a reaction at constant pressure.

q: The total energy absorbed for bond breaking in the reaction $	ext{H}_2	ext{(g)} + 	ext{Cl}_2	ext{(g)} ightarrow 2	ext{HCl(g)}$ is the sum of the bond energies of $	ext{H-H}$ and _____.
e: The total energy absorbed for bond breaking in the reaction extH2 ext(g) + extCl2 ext(g) ightarrow 2 extHCl(g) is the sum of the bond energies of extH-H and extCl-Cl. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Weight loss applications use Hess's law concept to calculate the number of _____ burned during a workout.
e: Weight loss applications use Hess's law concept to calculate the number of calories burned during a workout. Hess's law says the overall enthalpy change depends only on start and finish, not on the path you take.

q: Hand warmers produce heat from the _____ reaction.
e: Hand warmers produce heat from the exothermic reaction. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive. Isothermal: thermal energy is heat.

q: In burning fuels such as gasoline and propane, the _____ reaction takes place.
e: In burning fuels such as gasoline and propane, the exothermic reaction takes place. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive.

q: The endothermic reaction takes place during cooking food, baking bread, and _____ water.
e: The endothermic reaction takes place during cooking food, baking bread, and boiling water. An endothermic reaction absorbs heat from the surroundings, so the enthalpy change is positive.

q: Industries such as automobile manufacturers determine how much energy the engine consumes or generates while burning fuels by using _____ law.
e: Industries such as automobile manufacturers determine how much energy the engine consumes or generates while burning fuels by using Hess's law. Hess's law says the overall enthalpy change depends only on start and finish, not on the path you take.
